official.deadline_note: 2026 round deadline applied to BOTH applicants and referees (31 January 2026, Beijing Time). The 2027 call page had not been published under UCAS Financial Aids as of 10 October 2026; in earlier cycles the round opened in mid-to-late October, so a late-2026 opening is plausible but unconfirmed.
official.application_cycle: 2026 cycle: opened 15 October 2025, closed 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time); 2027 cycle not yet published
official.status_note: The 2026 CAS-ANSO Scholarship (Degree Program) round closed on 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time); UCAS and USTC notified results through their application systems or by email, and the ANSO Secretariat announced in June 2026 that evaluation (including the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO Scholarship) was complete. The UCAS Financial Aids listing still shows the 2026 call as the most recent CAS-ANSO call as of 10 October 2026, and the UCAS Deadline page still lists 2026-01-31.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full tuition waiver. UCAS's 2026 fee schedule sets master's tuition at RMB 30,000/year and PhD tuition at RMB 40,000/year (Science and Engineering) or RMB 34,000/year (Liberal Arts), and states that students awarded the CAS-ANSO Scholarship are exempt from tuition fees. The application fee is also waived for CAS-ANSO applicants.
official.funding_period: per month (doctoral); CNY 3,000 per month for master's
benefits: Tuition waiver for both the master's program and the PhD program

Monthly stipend for doctoral candidates of up to CNY 7,000 (CNY 6,000 or 7,000 depending on whether the qualification test has been passed, of which CNY 1,000 is provided by the CAS Institute), for up to 48 months
Monthly stipend of CNY 3,000 for master's candidates, for up to 36 months
One international travel allowance from the awardee's home country to China
One-time visa/residence permit allowance and application fee waiver
eligibility: Does NOT hold Chinese citizenship and holds a valid foreign passport
Friendly to China and abiding by the laws and decrees of China and UCAS rules and regulations
Master's program applicants: born after 1 January 1996 (inclusive); PhD program applicants: born after 1 January 1991 (inclusive)
Meets the admission criteria for international students of UCAS
Not currently pursuing a master's degree (for the master's program) or a doctoral degree (for the PhD program) at any university or institution in China
requirements: Meet the admission criteria for international students of UCAS for the 2026 Programs for International Students
Choose 'the CAS-ANSO Scholarship' in the UCAS online application
Tick the additional box to be considered as a candidate for the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship (PhD applicants only)
File and submit the application in the UCAS Online Admission System before the deadline
Applicants must NOT take up other assignments during the period of the scholarship
Applicants must not apply for the CAS-ANSO Scholarship through both USTC and UCAS simultaneously
documents: Scanned copy of passport information page (ordinary passport with at least one year of validity)
Two-inch recent bareheaded photo identical to the one used in the passport
Complete CV with detailed education and research experiences from university onwards, plus an employment certificate for currently employed applicants
Scanned copies of original degree certificates (bachelor's for master's applicants; master's and bachelor's for PhD applicants)
Scanned copies of original academic transcripts (undergraduate transcripts for master's applicants; master's and bachelor's transcripts for PhD applicants)
Scanned copy of a valid IELTS or TOEFL result or other proof of English proficiency (not required if the applicant's mother tongue is English)
Motivation letter stating purpose of study in China, academic background, reasons for applying, study plan and career goals; PhD applicants must also introduce their research experiences
Two reference letters from professors or associate professors on official institutional letterhead, signed and dated; the referee must not be the prospective UCAS supervisor
selection_criteria: UCAS enrols international students based on evaluation of application documents together with an entrance examination
The admission committee of the applicable UCAS school or CAS institute reviews documents and selects applicants for the entrance examination
The examination is mainly an interview; some colleges/institutes may require a written test
Merit-based selection on application materials review and admission examination results determines the final admission list
coverage: Tuition waiver for both the PhD program and the master's program (UCAS fee schedule waives tuition for CAS-ANSO awardees)
PhD monthly stipend: CNY 6,000 or 7,000 per month depending on whether the qualification test has been passed, of which CNY 1,000 is provided by the CAS Institute, for up to 48 months
Master's monthly stipend: CNY 3,000 per month, for up to 36 months
International travel allowance from the awardee's home country to China, one trip per awarded candidate

For ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship awardees, items 1 to 4 are sponsored by CAS and items 5 and 6, if eligible, are sponsored by TWAS/UNESCO; for all other CAS-ANSO Scholarship awardees, items 1 to 6 are covered by CAS
application_method: Log in to the UCAS Online Admission System for International Students at https://is.ucas.ac.cn/#/login
Firstly, choose 'the CAS-ANSO Scholarship' in the application
Secondly, tick the box to be considered a potential candidate for the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship, if relevant
File and submit the application in the system before the deadline (both applicants and referees had to complete their part by 31 January 2026, Beijing Time)
official.application_route: Apply online through the UCAS Online Admission System for International Students, selecting 'the CAS-ANSO Scholarship' in the form; referees submit their letters through the same system before the deadline.
official.study_mode: Degree program study with mandatory centralised training in Chinese language and Chinese culture plus all required credits, practical research and a degree thesis at UCAS colleges and schools or CAS institutes; the call does not publish a part-time option.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must NOT hold Chinese citizenship and must hold a valid foreign passport. Applicants who have given up original Chinese citizenship and become foreign citizens must provide documents certifying the cancellation of Chinese nationality.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students only: non-Chinese citizens holding a valid foreign passport, from all over the world. Note that any awardee on site in China at the time of application is not eligible for any travel subsidy.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction is published. The scholarship is administered at UCAS for study at UCAS colleges and schools or institutes of the Chinese Academy of Sciences; applicants who want the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship sub-category must additionally meet TWAS/UNESCO's developing-country criteria.
official.research_requirement: The UCAS route requires a motivation letter in which PhD applicants introduce their research experiences; no separate research proposal is required by the UCAS call. The USTC route of the same scholarship additionally requires a study or research proposal of no less than 1,000 words.
official.duration: Basic study period is commonly 3 years for master's degree students and 3-4 years for doctoral students. The scholarship duration is stated explicitly in the Admission Notice; the coverage table provides the doctoral stipend for up to 48 months and the master's stipend for up to 36 months.
official.description: The CAS-ANSO Scholarship (Degree Program), previously the ANSO Scholarship for Young Talents, is the postgraduate scholarship of the Alliance of National and International Science Organizations for the Belt and Road Regions (ANSO), sponsored by the Chinese Academy of Sciences and administered at UCAS for master's and PhD study. It supports 100 to 200 master's students and 300 PhD students every year across USTC, UCAS and CAS institutes around China, and includes the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship sub-category launched in 2022, under which TWAS/UNESCO selects up to 40 PhD students from developing countries each year, 10 prioritised for climate-related research.
official.region: Asia (China); hosted at UCAS and CAS institutes
official.program_type: Postgraduate degree program (master's and PhD research training)
official.english_requirement: Proficiency in English or Chinese is required. For English-taught programmes applicants must provide a scanned copy of a valid IELTS or TOEFL result or other proof of English proficiency; this is not necessary for applicants whose mother tongue is English. No minimum IELTS or TOEFL score is published. For Chinese-instructed programmes, Chinese proficiency must reach at least HSK Level 5 with no less than 180 scores.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the CAS-sponsored master's and PhD award for non-Chinese passport holders at UCAS, and the round that closed on 31 January 2026 was fully evaluated with results announced in June 2026, so the realistic target is the next cycle, which historically opens around mid-to-late October. Coverage is strong on paper - tuition waived plus a monthly stipend (3,000 CNY master's, up to 7,000 CNY doctoral) with medical insurance, one home-to-China airfare and a one-off visa allowance - but the money still leaves accommodation, meals and research extras on you. The application is a single UCAS online form in which you select 'the CAS-ANSO Scholarship', and your two referees must finish their letters in the same portal before the deadline, so referee chasing is the real scheduling risk.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Chinese master's and PhD applicants aged within the cut-offs (born after 1996 for master's, after 1991 for PhD) who want CAS-institute research capacity without self-funding, and who can line up two academic referees early.
application_readiness_checklist: Create the UCAS Online Admission System account and confirm your passport has at least one year of validity beyond the intended intake
Line up two professors or associate professors who are not your intended UCAS supervisor, and clear their availability for the referee step before the window opens
Get degree certificates and full transcripts colour-scanned as single PDFs per document, in English or Chinese or with a certified translation merged into the same file
Prepare a valid IELTS/TOEFL certificate unless your mother tongue is English, and an HSK 5 (180+) certificate if you intend to study a Chinese-taught programme
Draft the motivation letter separately for master's versus PhD, since PhD applicants must also document research experience
Select your host UCAS college or CAS institute and, if available, secure a Supervisor's Acceptance Form in advance - it is optional but strengthens the file
common_rejection_risks: Referee submissions missing the Beijing Time cut-off - the deadline explicitly covers referees, not just applicants
Applying through both USTC and UCAS at the same time, which the call states leads to disqualification
Being enrolled in a master's or doctoral programme at any institution in China at the corresponding level, which bars that level of the award
Certificates that are not in English or Chinese, or scans that are not colour scans of the original, which the fee schedule and materials rules treat as invalid
Creating more than one application account; UCAS checks for duplicates and disqualifies verified double submissions
Failing the annual review or qualifying examination after admission, which can terminate the scholarship and leave only an attendance certificate
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation is not waived - roughly RMB 30/day for a shared two- or three-person room and RMB 60/day for a single room - plus meals and daily living. The official fee schedule places board expenses, travel expenses and the costs of experiments, meetings and trainings beyond the programme curriculum at the student's own expense. Items 5 and 6 of the coverage table (travel and visa allowance) are reimbursed under the sponsor's own rules rather than paid up front.
document_audit: Reference letters must be on the referee's institution letterhead, signed and dated, and written by a professor or associate professor who is not your prospective UCAS supervisor
Every certificate and document must be in English or Chinese; if not, the original scan and its English or Chinese translation must be merged into one PDF, and colour scanning is specified
Only up to five published papers may be submitted, and unpublished work must not be sent - sending drafts actively hurts the file
Passport must be an ordinary passport with at least one year of validity; former Chinese citizens must also document cancellation of Chinese nationality
The two-inch photo must match the passport photo exactly
alerts: The 2026 round is closed and results were announced in June 2026 - anything marketed as an open CAS-ANSO application right now is not the official UCAS route
Deadlines are Beijing Time, and both the applicant and referee steps had to be completed by the cut-off, so plan for a time-zone gap
Applicants physically located in China when they apply receive no travel subsidy at all
Birth-date cut-offs roll forward each cycle; assume the 2027 round will shift the master's cut-off past 1997 and the PhD cut-off past 1992 and verify on the new call
You must choose between applying via USTC or via UCAS - dual applications void the candidacy
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online form in the UCAS Online Admission System: create the account, complete the profile and upload all documents, select 'the CAS-ANSO Scholarship' (and optionally the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO box), submit before the Beijing Time deadline, then prompt both referees to submit their letters through the same portal.
